title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: Sustinui — imputation must be in Scripture, here if anywhere
pass_a_gloss: I have borne your charge; see if you can bear mine. From here rises a stroke that overturns your view. You will grant me that the dogma of imputing Adam's actual to the whole human race, if true and to be believed, is taught somewhere in Scripture, our most absolute rule of faith. You will grant too that if taught anywhere, it is taught here, where Paul carefully lays out whatever evil flowed from Adam into the race. And you will grant at last that whatever evils Adam shared with his posterity Paul reduces to these two: sin and death.
pass_b_english: I have sustained your assault; see whether you can sustain mine. For from here rises for me an argument overturning your opinion. You will certainly grant me that dogma concerning the imputation of Adam's actual sin to the whole human race, if it is true, if it must be believed, is taught somewhere in Scripture, the most absolute norm of our faith. You will also grant that, if it is taught anywhere, it is taught in this place, where the Apostle accurately explains whatever evil flowed from Adam into the human race. You will grant at last that whatever evils Adam communicated with his posterity, those the Apostle reduces to these two, sin and death.
source_text: Sustinui impetum tuum, vide an possis meum. Hinc enim mihi surgit argumentum tuam evertens sententiam. Dabis mihi profecto dogma illud de imputatione peccati actualis Adami toti generi humano, si verum est, si credendum est, doceri alicubi in Scriptura absolutissima fidei nostrae norma. Dabis etiam, sicubi docetur, doceri in hoc loco, ubi Apostolus quicquid ab Adamo mali in humanum genus manavit explicat accurate. Dabis tandem quaecunque mala Adamus cum posteris suis communicavit, ea ab Apostolo revocari ad haec duo, peccatum & mortem.
